meta.label: Washing machines
tradeoffLabels: lower energy and water use per wash
built and legally supported to last
meta.attribution: Covers washing machines placed on the EU market, plus three ways to do laundry without buying a new one. Energy and water figures come from each model's own EU Product Information Sheet, published in the European Product Registry for Energy Labelling (EPREL) under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/2014. Every figure quoted is for the mandatory 'eco 40-60' programme, the single reference cycle EU law requires every washing machine to be tested and rated on, so the numbers are comparable across brands even though a household rarely runs that exact cycle. The environment score here is 100 minus the model's published Energy Efficiency Index (EEIW), so a lower index scores higher; the underlying kWh and litre figures are in each entry's own note. The longevity score comes from the same sheet's 'minimum duration of the guarantee offered by the supplier', converted to a 0-100 scale where 36 months would score 100. That figure sits on top of, not instead of, the two-year minimum consumer guarantee EU law provides on almost all goods sold in the EU regardless of what a supplier states on its own sheet. The durability score is France's mandatory durability index (indice de durabilite), which folds a repairability mark and a reliability mark into one score out of 10 and has applied to washing machines since April 2025; manufacturers publish the underlying filing on data.gouv.fr, the French government's open data platform, and this entry multiplies the published mark by ten. No EU-wide equivalent exists yet, so a durability score is only shown for the few models whose French filing could be matched to a specific machine; it describes the France-market registration of what is usually the same engineering platform sold under the same or a near-identical model name elsewhere in the EU. Beko, Whirlpool, Indesit and Hotpoint are now common brands of Beko Europe, the joint venture Arcelik and Whirlpool formed in April 2024 and which Arcelik now owns outright; they are kept as separate entries here because they are still sold, priced and positioned as separate lines. The launderette entry is sourced to a UK trade body and is marked UK rather than EU for that reason, though self-service laundries operate across Europe under other names. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: Bosch WGG254FLSN
products.description: A 10kg freestanding Bosch, made by BSH Hausgerate. Its EU energy label sits at the lower edge of class A, with water use and spin performance in the middle of this roster.

environment.note: Bosch WGG254FLSN's EU Product Information Sheet gives an Energy Efficiency Index of 51.7, energy efficiency class A, energy use of 0.511 kWh and water use of 50 litres per eco 40-60 cycle at rated 10kg capacity, with spin-drying efficiency class B at 1,351rpm and a noise class of B at 74dB in the spinning phase.

longevity.note: Bosch WGG254FLSN's EU Product Information Sheet states a minimum guarantee from the supplier of 24 months.

products.name: Haier HW90-B14939S8
products.description: A 9kg freestanding Haier. Its EU energy label shows the lowest spin noise of the class-A machines in this roster, at 67dB.

environment.note: Haier HW90-B14939S8's EU Product Information Sheet gives an Energy Efficiency Index of 52.0, energy efficiency class A, energy use of 0.494 kWh and water use of 48 litres per eco 40-60 cycle at rated 9kg capacity, with spin-drying efficiency class B at 1,400rpm and a noise class of A at 67dB in the spinning phase.

longevity.note: Haier HW90-B14939S8's EU Product Information Sheet states a minimum guarantee from the supplier of 24 months.

products.name: LG F2WR508S0W
products.brand: 8kg, lowest energy use among class-A entries
products.description: An 8kg freestanding LG. Its EU energy label shows the lowest energy and water use of the mainstream class-A machines in this roster, and the shortest eco cycle at 3 hours 38 minutes.

environment.note: LG F2WR508S0W's EU Product Information Sheet gives an Energy Efficiency Index of 46.2, energy efficiency class A, energy use of 0.420 kWh and water use of 48 litres per eco 40-60 cycle at rated 8kg capacity, with spin-drying efficiency class B at 1,160rpm, a programme duration of 3 hours 38 minutes, and a noise class of A at 71dB in the spinning phase.

longevity.note: LG F2WR508S0W's EU Product Information Sheet states a minimum guarantee from the supplier of 24 months.

products.name: Electrolux EW6SN427WI
products.description: A 7kg freestanding Electrolux and the weakest performer on efficiency in this roster, included because it is a mainstream model people buy, not because it scores well. Its supplier guarantee is also the shortest here, at 12 months.

longevity.note: Electrolux EW6SN427WI's EU Product Information Sheet states a minimum guarantee from the supplier of 12 months, the shortest of the models compared here.

products.name: Beko BM3WT3941W
products.description: A 9kg freestanding Beko, part of Beko Europe, the appliance group Arcelik now owns outright after buying out Whirlpool's stake in 2024. Its efficiency sits just inside class A, but its supplier guarantee is half the length of most other class-A entries here.

environment.note: Beko BM3WT3941W's EU Product Information Sheet gives an Energy Efficiency Index of 51.5, energy efficiency class A, energy use of 0.490 kWh and water use of 49 litres per eco 40-60 cycle at rated 9kg capacity, with spin-drying efficiency class B at 1,351rpm and a noise class of B at 75dB in the spinning phase.

longevity.note: Beko BM3WT3941W's EU Product Information Sheet states a minimum guarantee from the supplier of 12 months.

products.name: Indesit BTW S60400 EU/N
products.description: A narrow 40cm-wide, 90cm-tall top-loading Indesit built for utility cupboards too tight for a front loader. It is manufactured by Beko Europe, the same group behind Hotpoint. Its smaller 6kg drum, slower 951rpm spin and class C efficiency reflect that compact, budget positioning.

environment.note: Indesit BTW S60400 EU/N's EU Product Information Sheet gives an Energy Efficiency Index of 69.0, energy efficiency class C, energy use of 0.559 kWh and water use of 43 litres per eco 40-60 cycle at rated 6kg capacity, with spin-drying efficiency class C at 951rpm and a noise class of C at 78dB in the spinning phase; dimensions are listed as 90cm high and 40cm wide, a narrow top-loading format.

longevity.note: Indesit BTW S60400 EU/N's EU Product Information Sheet states a minimum guarantee from the supplier of 24 months across the EU generally, with stated exceptions of 12 months in Ireland and the United Kingdom, 36 months in Spain and Portugal, and 60 months in Norway.

products.description: A 9kg freestanding Miele, the only machine in this roster to reach spin-drying efficiency class A, at 1,600rpm. Faster spinning leaves laundry drier before any tumble dryer is used.

products.description: A narrow 41cm-wide, 86cm-tall top-loading Candy, made by Candy Hoover Group, which Haier now owns. It reaches class A efficiency despite the compact top-loading format that usually trades away efficiency for a smaller footprint.

environment.note: Candy TCA286TM5-S's EU Product Information Sheet gives an Energy Efficiency Index of 51.9, energy efficiency class A, energy use of 0.472 kWh and water use of 44 litres per eco 40-60 cycle at rated 8kg capacity, with spin-drying efficiency class B at 1,151rpm and a noise class of C at 77dB in the spinning phase; dimensions are listed as 86cm high and 41cm wide, a narrow top-loading format.

products.brand: 7kg narrow top loader, loudest spin here
products.description: A narrow 40cm-wide, 90cm-tall top-loading AEG, part of the Electrolux group. It reaches class A efficiency but is the loudest machine in this roster during the spin phase, at 79dB.

environment.note: AEG LTR8E373E's EU Product Information Sheet gives an Energy Efficiency Index of 51.9, energy efficiency class A, energy use of 0.447 kWh and water use of 44 litres per eco 40-60 cycle at rated 7kg capacity, with spin-drying efficiency class B at 1,251rpm and a noise class of C at 79dB in the spinning phase, the loudest of the models compared here; dimensions are listed as 90cm high and 40cm wide, a narrow top-loading format.

longevity.note: AEG LTR8E373E's EU Product Information Sheet states a minimum guarantee from the supplier of 24 months.

products.name: Hotpoint HB 93 Care
products.brand: 9kg, best efficiency and a matched durability filing
products.description: A 9kg freestanding Hotpoint, made by Beko Europe, and the most efficient machine in this roster by a wide margin. It is also the only model here whose France-market durability filing could be matched to the same platform's EU energy label, so it carries both an environment and a durability score.

environment.note: Hotpoint HB 93 Care UK's EU Product Information Sheet gives an Energy Efficiency Index of 36.2, energy efficiency class A, energy use of 0.344 kWh and water use of 49 litres per eco 40-60 cycle at rated 9kg capacity, the lowest energy use of any model in this roster, with spin-drying efficiency class B at 1,351rpm and a noise class of A at 72dB in the spinning phase.

products.name: Repairing the machine you have
products.description: Calling an independent repairer or a manufacturer service line instead of replacing the machine. EU law gives a repaired machine a long formal support tail: key spare parts must stay available for a decade, and repair information must reach professional repairers within two years of a model going on sale.

environment.note: The European Environment Agency reports that large household appliances, including washing machines, saw average lifespans rise 1.8 per cent a year from 11.6 years in 2019 to 12.5 years in 2023, and that extending product lifespans reduces the resource use, waste and emissions caused by replacing goods before they fail, though it also notes that 'replacement was preferred over repair, which was seen as too expensive' for large appliances.

longevity.note: Under EU Ecodesign Regulation 2019/2023, Annex II, manufacturers must make key spare parts, including the motor, drum, pumps, heating elements and circuit boards, available to professional repairers for 10 years after the last unit of a model is placed on the market, deliver ordered parts within 15 working days, and give professional repairers access to repair and diagnostic information from two years after a model's market placement.

accessibility.note: The same EU regulation requires repair and diagnostic information, including disassembly maps, wiring diagrams and fault codes, to reach professional repairers within two years of a model's market placement, which is what lets an independent repairer take on a job rather than only the manufacturer's own service network.

products.name: Secondhand and giveaway networks
products.brand: not a purchase, or a small one
products.description: Buying a used machine or taking one for free through a local giveaway network instead of buying new. Reuse avoids the resource and manufacturing footprint of a new appliance, at the cost of no manufacturer guarantee and no energy label for the specific unit.

environment.note: The European Environment Agency frames reuse and repair as ways to 'reduce the demand for new products', and states that premature disposal across the EU causes an estimated 261 million tonnes of CO2-equivalent emissions, consumes 30 million tonnes of resources and generates 35 million tonnes of waste each year, impacts that keeping a machine in use through resale or reuse avoids.

accessibility.note: Freecycle's own about page says its network has 'spread to more than 110 countries' and operates in '32 countries including the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, The United States, and all European Union countries', where members post things they no longer want for anyone nearby to collect for free.

products.name: Self-service launderette
products.brand: not a purchase, pay per wash
products.description: Using a coin- or app-operated launderette instead of owning a machine at all. The only option in this roster that needs no purchase, no installation and no plumbing work, which matters most for renters without a hookup.

accessibility.note: NALI, the UK trade association for self-service launderettes, says they serve 'students, those in rented accommodation with no machine provided, people with little time or inclination to launder at home and the elderly or disabled who are unable to manage it', and are 'a welcome saviour when the domestic machine breaks down', without the user buying, installing or maintaining any equipment.
